playbook:
When I'm dealt KING and I am to act first, I bet to build the pot and apply pressure.  
When I'm dealt KING and my opponent checks to me, I bet for value.  
When I'm dealt KING and my opponent bets into me, I generally call a single-chip bet (play K aggressively; don't fold K to one chip) unless a specific read or stack situation dictates otherwise.

When I'm dealt QUEEN and I am to act first, I usually bet to protect equity and apply pressure.  
When I'm dealt QUEEN and my opponent checks to me, I bet to try to take the pot.  
When I'm dealt QUEEN and my opponent bets into me, I call a single-chip bet rather than folding (Q is worth calling one chip), except in extreme stack/odds situations.

When I'm dealt JACK and I am to act first, I default to checking (avoid bluffing as the opener).  
When I'm dealt JACK and my opponent checks to me, I do not bluff routinely — I check rather than bet.  
When I'm dealt JACK and my opponent bets into me, I fold to a one-chip bet in most cases to protect my stack; only call with a concrete read or favorable pot odds.

When my opponent checks and the pot is small, prefer checking with marginal hands (J) and betting with strong/mid hands (K,Q).  
Adjust calls vs one-chip bets conservatively: call Q and K, fold J unless specific information or pot odds justify a call.

Always declare my actual card truthfully at showdown.
